tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
FROC score.

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

FROC is an evaluation metric that balances both sensitivity and false positives. It is widely used in medical image
analysis and previous MICCAI challenges. Average sensitivity with false positives of 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, based
on free-Response ROC (FROC) analysis, is used for evaluating the detection task.


Instance-level 3D bounding boxes are required to calculate a "hit". If a detection proposal has an IoU > 0.3 (the
degree of overlap of 3D bounding boxes is relatively low) with the ground truth, it counts for a “hit”.


Both sensitivity and false positives are important in this detection task.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

As FROC analysis is a whole-dataset evaluation, the detection rank is directly based on the FROC score. We adopt
the average sensitivity of FP= 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 as the ranking.


When a tie does happen between teams, we will check whether there is cheating in the solutions and if not, we will
manually decide the ranking based on the maximum recall in their solutions. If the maximum recalls are also the
same, we will finally decide the rankings according to the running efficiency. We will treat it as a tie only if both
FROC (average recall) and maximum recall are the same and there is no cheating between the two solutions,
although this would very unlikely happen.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

The missing results will be automatically counted by FROC analysis.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

FROC analysis is a whole-dataset evaluation, and it counts for both sensitivity and false positives. FROC is widely


 Mediastinal Lesion Analysis

used in medical image analysis and previous MICCAI challenges. We generally adopt the average sensitivity of
multiple FP values (FP= 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 is used in our challenge) as the ranking; it is difficult to obtain the
same results between teams.
